Do you mean the Apache Software Foundation (ASF)? Here’s a quick overview:

- What it is: A nonprofit (founded 1999) that oversees hundreds of open-source projects under “The Apache Way” of community-led, meritocratic governance.
- License: Most projects use the Apache License 2.0 (permissive, business-friendly, allows commercial use and distribution with attribution and notice).
- Governance: 
  - Projects are run by independent Project Management Committees (PMCs).
  - Contributors become Committers based on merit; PMC members handle releases and project direction.
  - New efforts start in the Apache Incubator to build community and process.
- How to contribute:
  - Join project mailing lists and issue trackers (most code now mirrored on GitHub under apache/).
  - Start with issues tagged “good first issue.”
  - Follow each project’s CONTRIBUTING guide; some contributions may require a Contributor License Agreement (CLA).
- Notable projects (a sample):
  - Web/serving: HTTP Server, Tomcat, Traffic Server
  - Big data: Hadoop, Spark, Kafka, Flink, HBase
  - Databases/storage: Cassandra, CouchDB, Iceberg, Parquet
  - Search/indexing: Lucene, Solr
  - Data/ML orchestration: Airflow, Beam, Superset
  - Messaging/streaming: Pulsar, ActiveMQ
  - Tools/libraries: Maven, Ant, Log4j, Commons, NetBeans, Camel
  - Office: OpenOffice
- Community and events: ApacheCon, local meetups, and virtual mailing-list–centric collaboration.
- Funding: Donations and sponsors support infrastructure and operations; projects remain community-driven.

Official site: https://www.apache.org
Project list: https://projects.apache.org
Incubator: https://incubator.apache.org

If you had something specific in mind—like how to contribute to a particular project, license details, or comparisons with other foundations—tell me what you’re looking for.
